title: Motivation montage
premise: No narrative. Effort, text, and the drop. The one that works when the footage is good and the story is thin.

copy.hook: Nobody is coming to save you
copy.cta: Send this to someone who needs it

shots.what: The single hardest-looking frame you own — strain, sweat, or the walk in
shots.subject: required
shots.shoot: Tight and slightly unstable. This is the only shot where handheld shake helps — it reads as urgency rather than sloppiness.

shots.what: Empty gym, or you alone in it
shots.subject: optional
shots.shoot: Wide and still, deliberately quiet after the hook. The contrast is the point.

shots.what: Effort, close — a face mid-set, veins, a grimace
shots.subject: required
shots.shoot: Get uncomfortably close. Wide shots of effort do not read; faces do.

shots.what: Effort, detail — chalk, a shaking bar, a hand on a knee
shots.subject: optional
shots.shoot: Shoot three of these. They are the cheapest shots to get and the ones a montage runs out of first.

shots.what: Effort, wide — the whole body working, room visible
shots.subject: required
shots.shoot: Walk an arc around the movement. An orbit gives the editor motion to match-cut on, which a locked-off wide never does.

shots.what: The heaviest, fastest, most violent thing in the session
shots.subject: required
shots.shoot: 4K60. Locked off, 45 degrees, whole body in frame. Everything before this exists to make this land.

shots.what: The moment after — the drop of the weight, the exhale, walking out
shots.subject: required
shots.shoot: Keep rolling. The release is what makes the effort mean anything.

shots.what: Something still — the empty rack, the door, you walking away
shots.subject: optional
shots.shoot: Uncluttered middle of frame, the text lives there. Hold five seconds.
